messages.content: We need a verified customer billing dataset ready for tomorrow morning's payroll and invoicing run.
I will prepare the dataset and verify it before the processing window.
Done means all required records are present, reconciliation passes, and the dataset is ready before morning processing.
I will track completeness, reconciliation, and deadline readiness.
The available source is a scanned report, so we started OCR plus manual correction.
The OCR/manual route is the current extraction plan.
After two hours, about 45 percent of rows are cleaned.
The cleanup is progressing but still incomplete.
A reconciliation sample shows roughly 6 percent mismatch.
Those mismatches need correction before the dataset is trusted.
Another hour of cleanup brings the dataset to about 70 percent complete.
Most rows have now passed through the OCR/manual workflow.
Mismatch is down to about 4 percent, mostly from account numbers and negative values.
The remaining errors are concentrated but still material.
Estimate: finishing the remaining OCR cleanup and full reconciliation will take about three more hours.
That estimate puts pressure on the morning processing deadline.
A new structured export has just been released by the source system. It includes all customer rows and original numeric fields.
That creates an alternative data source.
The structured export uses different column names, so adapting it will take about one hour including reconciliation.
Switching sources has a conversion cost but could reduce extraction error.
Some mappings already validated during OCR work can be reused with the structured export.
Part of the existing work can transfer even if the source changes.
The OCR team argues that abandoning a 70 percent complete pipeline would waste three hours of work.
There is substantial sunk effort in the current route.
The structured export has not yet been adapted, but its source values are machine-readable and complete.
The alternative appears higher quality but still requires integration and verification.
The morning run cannot be delayed, and unresolved reconciliation errors are not acceptable.
Both deadline and verification remain binding.
